clue.text: Stanley was the model for this modern officer (Gilbert)

definitions.text: Stanley was the model for this modern officer (Gilbert)

parts.words: Stanley was the model for this modern officer (Gilbert)
parts.note: in Gilbert and Sullivan's Pirates of Penzance, Stanley sings that he is the very model of a modern officer of high army rank

explanation.walkthrough: The clue quotes the famous patter song from The Pirates of Penzance, with W. S. Gilbert's lyrics; Stanley is the character who sings it.
explanation.definitionFit: Stanley in the operetta holds this senior army rank, ranking just below a lieutenant-general.

clue.text: Tape an old dance

explanation.definitionFit: A tape is a measuring device, and a stately dance of olden times was also called by this word.

clue.text: A flower Jack regarded as yours truly's

parts.note: J is the abbreviation for jack in a deck of cards
regarded as can be shortened to simply as
yours truly is the speaker, so yours truly's means belonging to me

explanation.surface: Someone named Jack admires a bloom he considers his own.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yours truly' is a jokey way of saying 'me', so the possessive gives the word meaning belonging to me.
explanation.definitionFit: Jasmine is a fragrant climbing shrub prized for its white or yellow blossoms.

clue.text: She'd scatter it in rows for the birds

indicators.note: the shuffled letters sit inside the word for rows

parts.note: ranks are rows, as of soldiers or seats

indicators.note: to scatter is to throw about, so the letters of the clue word get rearranged

explanation.surface: A woman will toss seed along the lines for the feathered visitors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scatter' turns SHED (from She'd) into EDSH, and 'in' puts that inside RANKS after its R.
explanation.definitionFit: Redshanks are wading shorebirds with bright scarlet legs.

clue.text: Run for the late edition

explanation.definitionFit: In cricket a run not scored off the bat is added to the total as a bonus; a special newspaper issue printed late is also known by this name.

clue.text: A self-admirer obtained one in the east of France

indicators.note: the pieces for obtained and one go inside the French word

parts.note: est is the French for east
obtained means got
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A vain person acquired a property in eastern France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the east of France' means the French word for east, EST, not a region; 'in' puts GOT and I inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone constantly preoccupied with themselves and their own importance admires their own person.

clue.text: Mobile state

parts.note: read not as a condition of being movable but as the US state containing the port city of Mobile

explanation.definitionFit: Mobile is a Gulf Coast port city in this southern US state.

clue.text: Clown crying 'help' in pantomime part

parts.note: a harlequin is a clown or buffoon in comic theatre

indicators.note: crying out a word means saying it aloud, so the sound is what counts here

parts.note: to help is to aid

explanation.surface: A clown shouts for assistance during his scene in a Christmas show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crying' signals that AID is spoken, giving the sound of ADE. In British pantomime, a seasonal family stage show, the harlequinade was the comic interlude featuring Harlequin.
explanation.definitionFit: The harlequinade was the slapstick section of a traditional British Christmas stage show.

clue.text: Collected boy after a service

indicators.note: the boy's name follows the earlier pieces

parts.note: a mass is a church service
Ed is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A lad was picked up after attending church.
explanation.definitionFit: To have gathered things together into a pile is to have accumulated them.

clue.text: Hard workers from any of nine cities

explanation.definitionFit: People who toil tirelessly are said to work like this; archaeologists found nine successive cities on the site of Troy.

clue.text: Wild cats likely at a place in Utah

indicators.note: wild means out of control, so these letters run riot into a new order

explanation.surface: Feral felines will probably be found somewhere in a western US state.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the state capital of Utah, beside the great saline lake.

clue.text: Rough-mannered student? Not in his novel

parts.note: L is a learner, the plate on a learner driver's car
something not in is out

indicators.note: novel means new, so the three letters take a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A coarse student does not appear in the author's book.
explanation.walkthrough: L for learner (student) is from the L-plate a British learner driver displays. 'novel' turns HIS into ISH.
explanation.definitionFit: A boorish, uncouth person behaves in a crude, ill-bred way.

clue.text: Cooked-up alibi covering Georgia's maid

indicators.note: the anagram wraps around the state abbreviation
cooked-up means fabricated, so the letters are reworked

parts.note: GA is the abbreviation for the US state of Georgia

explanation.surface: A servant from the South concocts a fake excuse to protect herself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cooked-up' turns ALIBI into ABIIL, and 'covering' wraps it around GA after its B and I.
explanation.definitionFit: This was an old literary term for a lady's personal servant, from a character in a 17th-century play.

clue.text: Pigtail for waiters

explanation.definitionFit: A plait of hair hanging behind was once called by this word, and it is also a line of people standing in turn.

clue.text: Strange thing to decline at the end of the day

indicators.note: strange means odd, so the letters of the next word are oddly rearranged

parts.note: to decline is to fall

explanation.surface: Something odd begins to wane as evening comes.
explanation.definitionFit: Dusk is when darkness descends, closing the daylight hours.

clue.text: Eg. slug an attractive person — and upset party drink

parts.note: a gas is slang for a delightful, highly enjoyable person or thing

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset turns the two words upside down, reading them from the bottom

parts.note: a do is a party
port is a fortified wine

explanation.surface: A charmer gets punched and knocks over the party drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns DOPORT round, giving TROPOD. The slang 'gas' for an enjoyable person is a stretch for attractive.
explanation.definitionFit: A slug is a mollusc of the class that crawls on a muscular foot, like snails.

clue.text: Sincere as characters making advances

indicators.note: the letters of the words are used as characters to build something new

explanation.surface: Earnest people, as personalities, are flirting.
explanation.definitionFit: To rise or grow larger is to go up, as prices advance.

clue.text: First son accepts suitable rank

indicators.note: one piece takes in the other, holding it inside

parts.note: Cain was the first son of Adam and Eve
apt means suitable

explanation.surface: The eldest boy takes on a fitting position.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a military or naval grade, an officer's level of seniority.

clue.text: In which a body may be thrown into the shade

definitions.text: In which a body may be thrown into the shade

parts.words: In which a body may be thrown into the shade
parts.note: a body here is a heavenly body, such as the moon or sun, darkened by another's shadow

explanation.definitionFit: An astronomical event when one celestial object blocks light from another darkens it.

clue.text: Dealings in a form of transport

explanation.definitionFit: To have no truck with something is to have no dealings with it; it is also a goods lorry.

clue.text: A tantrum first put on by artists

indicators.note: the word for tantrum comes first, before the letter A

parts.note: a temper is a fit of anger

explanation.surface: A fit of rage first shown by painters.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a paint made with egg yolk binder that painters apply.

clue.text: Peace-keepers never wrongly weaken in resolve

parts.note: UN, the United Nations, sends peace-keeping forces

indicators.note: wrongly means incorrectly arranged, so the letters are shuffled

explanation.surface: Peace-keeping troops never mistakenly lose their nerve.
explanation.definitionFit: To rattle someone is to deprive them of courage and composure.

clue.text: A scholar about to draw a Roman flask

indicators.note: the scholar's letters go around the next piece

parts.note: MA is a Master of Arts, a scholar
to draw is to pull

explanation.surface: An academic is about to sketch an ancient Roman bottle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like 'on the point of' with 'to draw'; it means around, putting PULL inside MA.
explanation.definitionFit: This was a two-handled vessel used in ancient Rome for oil or wine.

clue.text: Opposite the centre of Lincoln before morning?

indicators.note: the first name goes ahead of the morning abbreviation

parts.note: Abe was Abraham Lincoln's nickname

explanation.surface: Facing the middle of an English cathedral city just ahead of dawn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the centre of Lincoln' looks like a selection from the word; 'Opposite the centre' is the definition and Lincoln is the US president.
explanation.definitionFit: In nautical terms this means at right angles to a ship's middle, level with its side.

clue.text: Name, in modern Greek vernacular, of Latin origin

indicators.note: the abbreviation for name goes inside the language term

parts.note: Romaic is the old name for the everyday spoken modern Greek language

explanation.surface: A word in everyday modern Greek that actually comes from Latin.
explanation.definitionFit: Romance languages derive from Latin, and this term describes them.

clue.text: Illustration showing former member in the drink

parts.note: ex means former

indicators.note: the member goes inside the drink

parts.note: ale is a drink
MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A picture reveals an ex-politician in the water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the drink' suggests the sea, as in slang; here it is ALE.
explanation.definitionFit: A specimen or instance used to show what something is like illustrates a point.

clue.text: Pantomime character is Mole? Rubbish

parts.note: a mole is a breakwater or jetty, a pier
rot means rubbish or nonsense

explanation.surface: Is the burrowing animal a figure in a stage show? Nonsense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mole' looks like the animal, perhaps from a children's play; it is a harbour wall.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a sad white-faced clown figure from French comic theatre.

clue.text: Act as go-between for the compound

explanation.definitionFit: To mediate is to step in between parties; in chemistry, a substance formed between starting materials and product.
